evidence: Option (D): the fixed-path instance of the volume-type defect, on a branch off origin/main (7f7bddd), touching no queued PR. THE DEFECT, MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED: every memory file was guarded by existsSync and then handed to readFileSync. At .claude/memory/DECISIONS.md a DIRECTORY gives EISDIR with a raw stack trace; a FIFO NEVER RETURNS — exit 142 at 8,016 ms under an 8s perl alarm. check:memory is a BLOCKING CI step, where a crash names itself and a hang reads as a slow build. SIX read sites, not three: the --json branch re-read all three paths with the same unguarded pair, a second copy of the same defect reachable only with --json; it now reuses what the checks loaded. SCAN/GUARD VERDICT — THE SPLIT DOES NOT APPLY, ESTABLISHED BY READING THE FILE: it creates nothing (no writeFileSync, appendFileSync, mkdirSync, renameSync, rmSync, unlinkSync, openSync), so "is this path free to CREATE?" is never asked and the non-resolving predicate is not wanted here. The one question it does ask MUST resolve, so statSync — a symlinked memory file is content that must still be measured. NOT ASSERTED: two controls pin it and go red under lstatSync. NOTHING IS NEWLY SKIPPED. The dangling-symlink path is deliberately unchanged — existsSync follows links, so a broken one is already absent and already refused as missing-file; a control asserts it is NOT re-routed through the new refusal, and that control is stable across all three script variants. ONE ROW NARROWS, measured on both versions: a symlink to a character device (/dev/null) previously read as 0 bytes and PASSED, and is now refused. The absent state is deliberately NOT recorded as a problem field, because absent is normal for the optional archive and the required files already fail as missing-file. NON-VACUITY, BOTH DIRECTIONS: new cases against the ORIGINAL script — 18 tests, 13 pass, 5 fail, with the three FIFO cases each hitting the 8s cap at 8,010 / 8,013 / 8,006 ms, which is the hang reproduced three times; with statSync replaced by lstatSync and nothing else changed — 16 pass, 2 fail, EXACTLY the two symlink controls and nothing else. Fixed script: 18 pass, 0 fail. One caveat stated rather than hidden: the symlinked-file-is-still-read control fails against the original on a SCHEMA assertion (the problem key is absent there), not on a behavioural one. SUITES, MEASURED IN MY OWN WORKTREE AND NEVER AT THE SESSION ROOT: npm run check 43 of 43 passed, 0 failed, 85.3s; memory-budget 18 pass 0 fail, up from 11 before the 7 new cases; the existing 11 passed unchanged against the fix before any new case was added. CARRIED IN BY INSTRUCTION: the test helper's JSON.parse of stdout had no emptiness check — the THIRD instance of the shape found on #99 — so every induced crash surfaced as "Unexpected end of JSON input"; it now names root, exit and stderr. RESIDUAL FLAGGED NOT FIXED, BY INSTRUCTION: a TOCTOU window between statSync and readFileSync; the same window exists in scripts/evict-memory.mjs.
